label: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017
output:
To: lindqvist-family-blog
Replying to: none
Cc: none
Subject: Fernhollow Photo is officially a real business (deep breath)

Okay, deep breath. Fernhollow Photo is officially a real business. Like, LLC real. Website real. Bookings real. I’m writing this here first because Thanksgiving at Aunt Ruthie’s is in two weeks and I would very much like to not have this come out over the turkey while Dad gives his famous health insurance speech to a captive audience.

Dad, since I know you’re reading this with your reading glasses on and a comment already forming: I picked a marketplace plan on November 5. It starts January 1. I’m covered. You can save the speech for someone who needs it. I love you.

Here’s the short version of how this happened. Rosebud Lane closed at the end of October. Marisol told me on October 6. I shot for her for four years, and I’m grateful for every one of them. I’m not going to pretend that wasn’t a lot to process. It was. But it’s also the push I needed to stop saying “someday” and make it real.

I filed the LLC on October 22 on my lunch break, in my car outside a Fred Meyer. Then I cried a little. Not sad crying. Just big-feelings crying while a guy in the next spot loaded groceries into his trunk. The website went live November 1. So yes, this is happening.

Here’s the part that makes me feel like this is actually a plan and not just me with a laptop and too many lens caps: I already have 14 weddings booked for 2027. Six of those are Marisol referrals. Eight found me on my own. Eight! I’m not totally sure my brain has caught up to that yet. June is already busy, and the farthest one so far is Wallowa Lake in September.

The first booking that was 100% mine was Dahlia and Ken at Timberline on June 12. They found me through the Multnomah Falls couple photos. I did a little dance in my kitchen when the deposit came in. Pickle was concerned. Sam was not surprised.

Jae is second shooting the big weddings with me and getting paid per wedding, which means I’m not doing this alone with three cameras and a granola bar. I’m also not being reckless here. I’ve been planning this in my head for two years. I know it looks sudden from the outside, but it really, really isn’t. I have bookings on the books, a second shooter, insurance, and a budget I’ve been staring at for months.

It is scary. I’m not going to pretend it isn’t. Being responsible for my own bookings and taxes and insurance and all of it is a lot. But it’s the good kind of scary. The kind where the scary part and the excited part are kind of holding hands. I’m asking you to be excited with me, not worried for me. I’ve got the worrying covered. I need a cheering section.

Marisol deserves a huge shoutout here. She basically taught me everything I know about this work. She handed me six couples for 2027 and told me I was ready before I fully believed her. Marisol, thank you. I don’t know how to make that sound big enough in a family blog post, but I mean it.

The name Fernhollow comes from the fern hollow trail behind Grandma’s old place in Gresham. That’s where I took my first real pictures with her Pentax. Grandma, the name is for you. I think about that trail every time I say the business name, and I hope you know how much those afternoons meant to me.

Sam made a cake to celebrate. It said FERNHOLLOW. He spelled it FERNHOLOW. We ate it anyway. It was a good cake. He’s been really great about all of this, including the part where I talk about lighting for 45 minutes and the part where our dining table is now a shipping station.

So that’s the news. Fernhollow Photo is real. I’m nervous and excited and probably going to cry at Thanksgiving, but in a good way. Please be excited with me. I’m happy to answer questions, and I promise I’ve thought about the hard parts more than this post makes it sound.

One more thing: I’ll bring my camera to Ruthie’s. If anyone wants free family pictures while we’re there, grab me. Seriously. No charge, no pressure, just let me know and I’ll make sure we get one of the whole group. Sam and I will be there with rolls and the cranberry thing. See you in Salem.

Love you all,
Tessa
